#20 Ms: tenodaŚ; #21 Ist hier "bhaṭitraṃ" (pw: 'am Spiesse gebacken',
Bhāvaprakāśa 2.20) zu lesen? - A/W: 'The word is obviously a Sanskritization. It
could be that it refers to "bhaṭurā/baṭurā" (from "bhaṭṭhā/bhaṭṭhi" 'kiln, oven'

eatable exactly. The same dictionaries explain "śikhariṇī" as a dish made of curds,
sugar, and spices, but the obvious cognate "śikaraṇ" current in Marathi stands
primarily for crushed bananas or plantain fruits mixed with milk and sugar'.; #22 Ś:

anticipated in Trikāṇḍī/Vākyapadīya 3.7.82 as Helārāja's introduction to the
Kārikā indicates. The "iti" occuring in the line is clearly not intended as indicative
of a direct quotation (anyone who has; #53 Ms: Śmaive; #54 N: om.; #55 Ś: anya;
#56 Ś: Śkri[3 Akṣaras zerstört].; #57 Ś: atra; #58 Ś:ŚābhiŚ[5 Akṣaras zerstört].; #59

grammar. There is frequently no difference in spirit between the mnemonic verses
of these texts and the (apparently popular grammar) verses cited in works such as

[4.2.2.]
  SD
dvitīyā tu guṇakriyā yā pradhānakriyānirvartanasamakālam eva nirvartyate. ta-
syāṃ niyamena śantṛṅṅānaś ityādayo bhavanti /
children.translated_text:
[4.2.2.]
SD (prose commentary)
The second [type of] subordinate action (<s>guṇakriyā</s>) is one that is accomplished simultaneously with the accomplishment of the principal action (<s>pradhānakriyā</s>). In that case, [suffixes] such as <s>śatṛ</s>, <s>ṅ</s>, <s>ānaś</s>, and the like necessarily apply.
SP (verse)
The subordinate action (<s>guṇakriyā</s>) is accomplished simultaneously with the principal action;

children.text: śantrādyantā dvitīyā sā. 'sa gacchati paṭhan' yathā //
children.translated_text: that second [type], ending in <s>śatṛ</s> and the like—as in '<s>sa gacchati paṭhan</s>' (he goes while reciting). //

children.text: #69tyādyantaiva kriyā mukhyā tv. anyā mukhyāṅgatāṃ bhajet /
children.translated_text: Only an action ending in [suffixes like <s>śatṛ</s>] and the like is the principal action; the other assumes subordination to the principal. //
Some <s>kṛdanta</s> (verbal derivative) action is equal to the principal, [and acts as principal] in the absence of that [principal]. //

[4.2.2.1.]
  SD
guṇapradhānabhāvaś ca vaktṛvivakṣākalpito, na tu vāstavaḥ, yathā 'bhuktvā gac-
chati, gatvā bhuṅkte / pacan bhuṅkte, bhuñjānaḥ pacati. paṭhan gacchati, gacchan
paṭhati. gāyan gacchati, gacchan (17r:) gāyati' ity.
children.translated_text:
[4.2.2.1.]
SD (prose commentary)
And the relation of subordination and principalness (<s>guṇapradhānabhāva</s>) is determined by the speaker's intention (<s>vaktṛvivakṣā</s>), not by reality. As in '<s>bhuktvā gacchati</s>' (having eaten, he goes), '<s>gatvā bhuṅkte</s>' (having gone, he eats); '<s>pacan bhuṅkte</s>' (he eats while cooking), '<s>bhuñjānaḥ pacati</s>' (he cooks while eating); '<s>paṭhan gacchati</s>' (he goes while reciting), '<s>gacchan paṭhati</s>' (he recites while going); '<s>gāyan gacchati</s>' (he goes while singing),

[4.3.1.]

yatra tu kriyāpadaṃ kiṃcit svarūpeṇa nopāttaṃ #79, tatrāstir bhavantīparo [']dhy-
āhriyata #80 iti bhāṣyakāravacanaprāmāṇyāt #81 asti, bhavati, vidyate iti vā sattā-
sāmānyavāci kriyāpadam adhyāhṛtya, vākyārthapratiṣṭhāne[na] #82 bhāvyam.
sattā hi sarvabhāvānām antaraṅgā, yathā 'vṛkṣa' iti kevalapade ukte, asti,
bhavati, vidyate iti vā gamyate. (17v:) atra vā astīti kriyāsāmānyavāci
dhātūpalakṣaṇaparam.
children.translated_text:
[4.3.1.]
SD (prose commentary)
But where some verbal form is not employed in its own form, there, on the authority of the <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s>'s statement that "<s>asti</s> (is), <s>bhavati</s> (becomes), [or <s>vidyate</s> (exists)] is supplied," a verbal form denoting general existence (<s>sattāsāmānyavācin</s>) such as <s>asti</s>, <s>bhavati</s>, or <s>vidyate</s> [is understood].
SP (verse)

children.translated_text: The verb <s>asti</s> (to be) should be supplied where no verb is heard; /

children.text: 'prāpnoti sa naro mokṣaṃ, yasya bhaktir harau' #83 yathā //
children.translated_text: as in '<s>prāpnoti sa naro mokṣaṃ, yasya bhaktir harau</s>' (that man attains liberation who has devotion to <s>Hari</s>). //

children.text:
[4.3.2.]
  SD
kvacic ca prakaraṇānusāreṇa viśiṣṭāpi kriyādhyāhriyate, kartṛrahitāyāḥ
kriyāyā abhāvāt.
children.translated_text:
[4.3.2.]
SD (prose commentary)
And sometimes, in accordance with the context, even a specific verb is supplied, because an action without an agent does not exist.

children.text:
[5.]
  SD
evaṃ evaṃbhūtaṃ vākyaṃ kvacin muktaka ekaṃ bhavati, kvacid dve vākye, kvacid
bahūni vākyāni / prabandhe tu bahūny eva vākyāni bhavanti. teṣāṃ ca vākyā-
nāṃ parasparasambaddhatopādeyā, na ced unmattavākyatvaprasaṅgāt, yathā
'kuṇḍam a(18r:)jājinaṃ palalaṃ sphaiyakṛtasya #84 putra' iti #85.
children.translated_text:
[5.]
SD (prose commentary)
Thus, a sentence of this nature is sometimes a single independent sentence (<s>muktaka</s>), sometimes two sentences, sometimes many sentences. In continuous discourse (<s>prabandha</s>), however, there are indeed many sentences. And their mutual connection (<s>parasparasambaddhatā</s>) is to be adopted; if not,
SP (verse)

children.text: evaṃbhūtaṃ kvacid vākyam ekaṃ, dve vā, bahūni vā /
children.translated_text: A sentence of this nature is sometimes one, or two, or many, /

children.text: vaktum arthaṃ samarthāni, sambandhaś cet parasparam /
children.translated_text: [and they are] capable of expressing [their] meaning, if there is mutual connection; /
otherwise, [the result would be] the madness [of utterances like] '<s>kuṇḍaṃ palālam</s>' (a pot, straw). //

***NOTES:
#84 Ms: <s>spheyaŚ</s>; #85 Cf. <s>Mahābhāṣya</s> 1.1.1 (p.38);

children.text:
[5.1.]
  SD
parasparasambandhaś ca svaśabdanirdiṣṭārthamukhena #86 vā bhavati,
sarvanāmaparāmṛṣṭārthamukhena vā.
children.translated_text:
[5.1.]
SD (prose commentary)
And the mutual connection is either through the meaning indicated by one's own word (<s>svaśabdanirdiṣṭārthamukhena</s>), or through the meaning referred to by a pronoun (<s>sarvanāmaparāmṛṣṭārthamukhena</s>).

***NOTES:
#86 Ms: <s>ŚniṣṭārthaŚ</s>;

children.text:
[5.1.1.]
  SD
svaśabdanirdiṣṭārthamukhena samanvaye bahavaḥ prakārāḥ, tathā hi yattador
upakramopasaṃhārakramarūpo nityam abhisambandhaḥ. sa ca śābdaḥ, ārthaś ca.
children.translated_text:
[5.1.1.]
SD (prose commentary)
In the case of connection through the meaning indicated by one's own word, there are many modes. For instance, the connection of <s>yat</s> and <s>tat</s> (relative and correlative), which has the form of a fixed sequence of introduction and conclusion, is invariable. And it is of two kinds: verbal (<s>śābda</s>) and semantic (<s>ārtha</s>).

children.text:
[5.1.1.1.]
  SD
dvayor #87 yattador upādāne sati, śābdaḥ.
children.translated_text:
[5.1.1.1.]
SD (prose commentary)
When both <s>yat</s> and <s>tat</s> are employed [in the sentence], it is verbal.
SP (verse)
The connection of <s>yat</s> and <s>tat</s>, which has the form of a sequence of introduction and conclusion, /

children.text: yaḥ sambandhaḥ, sa śābdo hi. dvayoḥ śabdena kīrtanam //
children.translated_text: that connection is indeed verbal—[it is] the mention of both through [their respective] words. //

***NOTES:
#87 Ms: <s>dvayo</s>;

[5.1.1.2.]
SD (prose commentary)
When only one of the two is employed, it is semantic.
SP (verse)
Where there is the employment of only one of <s>yat</s> or <s>tat</s>, /
the implied reference (<s>ākṣepa</s>) of the other, due to the invariable connection, is called semantic. //

children.text:
[5.1.1.2.1.]
  SD
yadi tasyārthasāmarthyenākṣepāt tacchabdasya #88 kevalopādāne saty, ārthaḥ
(18v:) triprakāraḥ, prasiddhaprakrāntānubhūtavastuviṣayeṇa ca, yacchabdena tasya
sambandhāt.
children.translated_text:
[5.1.1.2.1.]
SD (prose commentary)
If, by the force of the meaning, through implied reference, only one of the <s>tat</s>-word pair is employed, the semantic [connection] is of three kinds: with reference to a well-known object, to a previously mentioned object, and to an experienced object, through the connection of <s>yat</s>-word with it.
SP (verse)

children.text: ākṣepo [']rthād yado yatra nopādānaṃ #89, tadas tadā /
children.translated_text: Where the implied reference is from meaning, and <s>yat</s> is not employed, then <s>tat</s> [is used] at that point; /
the semantic [connection] is threefold: with reference to the well-known, the experienced, and the previously mentioned. //

***NOTES:
#88 Ms: <s>tat tacchadśabdasya</s>; #89 Ś: <s>tūpādānaṃ</s>;

children.text:
[5.1.1.2.2.]
  SD
yacchabdasya kevalasyopādāne sati, ārtho dvividhas samanvayaḥ, prakrāntavastu-
viṣayeṇa kalpitakarmādiviṣayeṇa ca, tacchabdena tasya sambandhāt.
children.translated_text:
[5.1.1.2.2.]
SD (prose commentary)
When only the <s>yat</s>-word is employed, the semantic connection (<s>samanvaya</s>) is twofold: with reference to a previously mentioned object and with reference to an imagined object such as <s>karman</s> and the like, through the connection of <s>tat</s>-word with it.
SP (verse)
When only <s>yat</s> is employed, with reference to the previously mentioned, that /
semantic [connection] is twofold: also with reference to the imagined object such as action and the like. //
And the reference to an agent stated within the same sentence (<s>ekavākya</s>) by [demonstratives such as] <s>idam</s> and the like, /

children.text: tacchabdena parāmarśo na kāryaḥ kavibhiḥ kvacit //
children.translated_text: should never be made by poets through the <s>tat</s>-word. //

children.text: ya ekasya yadaḥ pūrvaṃ prayogo, duṣṭa eva saḥ /
children.translated_text: The use of <s>yat</s> alone before [its correlative] is indeed faulty; /
for when there is the use of <s>idam</s> and the like, synonymous in meaning [with <s>tat</s>], /

children.text: yadaḥ pūrvaṃ prayoge ca, no doṣo, na #93 guṇas tadā //
children.translated_text: and [<s>yat</s> is] used first, there is neither a fault nor a merit. //

***NOTES:
#90 N: <s>Śviṣaye na</s>; #91 SPS: "<s>tat</s>" means <s>tadā</s>; #92 N: <s>kalpitas tatkarmādiviṣaye na ca</s>; #93 N: <s>na</s> in margina.;

children.text:
[5.2.]
  SD
kvacic ca kevale kriyāpade 'dhyāhriyamāṇakārakasambandhe sati, vākyārthapari-
samāptir dṛśyate / yathā 'āgaccha, āgaccha. cala, cala. brūhi, brūhi. yāhi, yāhi.
apasarpa, apasarpa. vada, vada'.
children.translated_text:
[5.2.]
SD (prose commentary)
And sometimes, when the connection of the <s>kāraka</s> (case relation) being supplied is with the verbal form alone, the completion of sentence-meaning (<s>vākyārthaparasamāpti</s>) is observed. As in '<s>āgaccha, āgaccha</s>' (come, come); '<s>cala, cala</s>' (move, move); '<s>brūhi, brūhi</s>' (speak, speak); '<s>yāhi, yāhi</s>' (go, go); '<s>apasarpa, apasarpa</s>' (withdraw, withdraw); '<s>vada, va[da]</s>' (say, say).
SP (verse)
And the syntactic relation of implied <s>kārakas</s> (case-relations) may sometimes occur
even in the employment of a single action, as in 'Speak! Go away, sir!'

***NOTES:
#94 N: -kriyā-;

children.text: atra cai(19r:)kena ślokena vākyārthaparisamāptau muktakaṃ, dvābhyāṃ ślokā-
children.translated_text: Here, when the sentence-meaning is completed in a single verse, it is a <s>muktaka</s> (independent verse); when the sentence-meaning is completed

children.text: bhyāṃ #95 vākyārthaparisamāptau yugalakam, tribhis tilakam, caturbhis cakka-
children.translated_text: in two verses, it is a <s>yugalaka</s> (couplet); in three, a <s>tilaka</s> (ornament-trio); in four, a <s>cakka-</s>

children.text: lakam, pañcabhiḥ kulakam, anantaraṃ mahākulakam // etair vyastais samastair vā
children.translated_text: <s>laka</s> (quartet); in five, a <s>kulaka</s> (cluster); beyond that, a <s>mahākulaka</s> (great cluster). By these, whether separate or combined,
a <s>prabandha</s> (literary composition) [is formed]. Thus, auspiciousness.

[5.3.]
  SD (Prose redaction)
SP (Verse redaction)
Where the repose of the sentence-meaning is seen in a single verse,

children.text: muktakaṃ tatra #97, yugmena yugalam, tilakaṃ tribhiḥ //
children.translated_text: there it is a <s>muktaka</s> (independent verse); with a pair, a <s>yugala</s> (couplet); with three, a <s>tilaka</s> (trio).

children.text: caturbhiś ca cakkalakaṃ, pañcabhiḥ kulakaṃ smṛtaṃ /
children.translated_text: With four, a <s>cakkalaka</s> (quartet); with five, it is known as a <s>kulaka</s> (cluster);
the masters speak of a <s>mahākulaka</s> (great cluster) beyond that.

children.text:
***NOTES:
#95 Ms: vākyābhyāṃ; #96 Ś: padyenaiŚ; #97 N: tatra bis cakkalakam in margina.;
children.translated_text:
***NOTES:
#95 Ms: vākyābhyām; #96 -: padyenai-; #97 N: tatra bis cakkalakam in the margin;
SD (Prose redaction)
This mere indication of syntactic construction (<s>anvaya</s>) has been illuminated for beginners.
By this direction, beginners become confident in proper syntactic construction.

children.text: pañcake daśake vāpi ślokānāṃ yadi darśyate /
children.translated_text: If it is demonstrated in groups of five or even ten verses,

children.text: bālaś caitat, tatas samyaganvayam #98 prati muktadhīḥ //
children.translated_text: even a beginner, from that, [becomes] one whose mind is liberated with regard to proper syntactic construction.
Thus the <s>Samanvayadik</s> (Direction on Syntactic Construction) is concluded. This is the work of the scholar <s>Chuḍḍaka</s> (Kuḍaka), the king's paṇḍita.
SP (Verse redaction)
This <s>Samanvayapradīpa</s> (Lamp of Syntactic Construction), following the path stated by <s>Kuḍaka</s>, by me
has been shown. The learned should here supply what has been missed.
(Commentary:) '<s>Kuḍaka</s>' is a certain scholar. 'The path stated by him' means the specific treatise

children.text: samanvayadigākhyo #100 granthaviśeṣa ity arthaḥ. sa tu gadyarūpeṇa sthito,
children.translated_text: called <s>Samanvayadik</s> — this is the meaning. That [treatise] stands in prose form,
while this [version] is in verse form — just this is the only difference. This

children.text:
samanvayapradīpasaṅketaḥ vibudhasamūhavanditapādapadmasya
śrīgaṅgādharasvāminaḥ śiṣyeṇa paṇḍitadevaśarmaṇā iti bhadram #101.
children.translated_text: <s>Samanvayapradīpa</s> compendium is concluded, [composed] by the scholar <s>Devaśarman</s>, disciple of the illustrious <s>Gaṅgādharasvāmin</s>, whose lotus-feet are venerated by assemblies of the learned. Blessings.
